headline: Verify Timberline and Sno-Park Permit Requirements
reservation: Mount Hood National Forest does not currently use a general entry reservation system, but specific areas like Sno-Parks in winter or certain campgrounds require permits or fees. Timberline Lodge and ski areas have independent booking systems; check the official Forest Service site to distinguish between parking fees and recreational permits.

days.title: Historic Timberline and Southern Slopes

stops.name: Timberline Lodge
stops.detail: Examine the 1930s craftsmanship and stonework of this National Historic Landmark situated at the tree line.

stops.name: Trillium Lake
stops.detail: Walk the shoreline trail for the classic view of the summit reflected in the water, following posted signs for kayak launch areas.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; frequent stops for photography and grades
days.note: US 26 can experience heavy traffic on weekends; weekdays offer a quieter pace.

days.title: Orchards and Northern Vistas

stops.name: Fruit Loop Orchards
stops.detail: Drive through the valley for mountain views framed by pear and apple trees, stopping at seasonal farm stands.

stops.name: Lost Lake
stops.detail: Visit this northern-side destination for a different perspective of the peak and old-growth forest surroundings.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours; winding rural roads with varied surfaces
days.note: Check OR 35 road conditions if traveling during the spring or fall shoulder seasons.

days.title: River Valleys and Alpine Air

stops.name: Salmon River Trail
stops.detail: Follow the lower elevation path through ancient cedar and Douglas fir forests along the designated Wild and Scenic river.

stops.name: Mount Hood Meadows
stops.detail: Visit for seasonal summer hiking or winter snow sports, checking their official site for lift operating schedules.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; conditions vary with mountain weather
days.note: Traction tires or chains may be required by law on mountain passes from November through April.

intel.title: Lake Access
intel.text: Trillium Lake parking fills early on summer days; arrive before peak hours or have a secondary forest site planned. Designated parking passes must be displayed.

intel.title: Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell coverage is spotty along OR 35 and nonexistent at many trailheads like Lost Lake. Carry physical maps for navigation beyond the main highways.

intel.title: Corridor Services
intel.text: Sandy and Government Camp provide fuel and food on the south side, while Hood River serves the north. Plan fuel stops before entering forest service roads.

intel.title: Ski vs Hiking
intel.text: Timberline offers summer skiing, but hiking trails near the lodge remain snow-covered until late July. Confirm trail readiness with ranger reports.

intel.title: Permit Checks
intel.text: Digital permits are often required for specific backcountry zones; verify current requirements at the Zigzag Ranger Station or official website.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Portland International Airport (PDX) and pick up your vehicle; Sandy is the primary supply town for groceries and gear before entering the Zigzag area.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle is fine for US 26, but high-clearance is better for the Lost Lake approach; check rental policies regarding snow chain use.
plan.goldenHour: Trillium Lake is a renowned sunrise location, though morning mist and seasonal cloud cover often obscure the mountain face.
